results.content: A fresh round of polling is flashing new warning signs for President Donald Trump and Republicans ahead of the midterm elections. With control of Congress on the line, surveys released this week found Trump's approval rating near second-term lows while Democratic voters reported significantly greater enthusiasm about voting in November. One of the clearest warning signs for Republicans came from a Reuters/Ipsos survey released this week. Just 39% said they were satisfied with the direction of the country, down from 65% at the start of Trump's term and the lowest level recorded during his second presidency. results.content: With highly contested midterm elections in a few weeks, President Donald Trump again sees his approval rating stuck at a career-low in Reuters/Ipsos polling, which also indicated cratering support from Hispanic voters. The new poll, released on Monday, Oct. 5, found that only 32% of Americans approved of the president’s job performance. Trump’s current approval rating, which has now sat at 32% in two consecutive polls, is the lowest he has seen in Reuters/Ipsos polling during both terms in office.
